title: IB approaches & studies
examples: How do these approaches differ when explaining memory?
Can one approach explain all human behaviour?
Which approach do you think is most useful today?

explain.say: Today we look at three ways to study the mind. These are the biological, cognitive, and sociocultural approaches.
The biological approach looks at the body's physical parts. It suggests brain structures and genes play a big role.
The cognitive approach focuses on mental processes like thinking and memory. It treats the mind like information processing.
The sociocultural approach emphasizes that culture and social interaction shape us. We learn from the people around us.
For example, if someone struggles with language, the cognitive approach might look at their language centers in the brain.
A real-life example is understanding why rituals differ across countries. Culture dictates the behaviour.

faq.q: How do these approaches interact with each other?
faq.a: They are not always separate boxes. Many psychologists use different approaches to get a complete picture of behaviour. You could also ask how they overlap.
asks: Can I use more than one approach?

faq.q: Which approach is considered the most scientific?
faq.a: All approaches use scientific methods, but the biological approach often uses measurable tools like brain scans. You might also ask which one is best.
asks: Is one approach better than the others?
Which one has the most evidence?

faq.q: Does the biological approach only look at animals?
faq.a: No, it applies to humans too. It examines the human brain and its biological makeup. You could also ask about human biology.
asks: Is it limited to physical science?

faq.q: What is meant by 'sociocultural' in psychology?
faq.a: It means looking at how the society and culture influence our thoughts and actions. Think about how your family teaches you things. You could also ask about cultural influence.
asks: What is the role of culture?

faq.q: Can a cognitive approach explain emotion?
faq.a: It can, by suggesting emotions are linked to how we interpret events. For example, we might think an event is dangerous. You could also ask about emotional processing.

facts: The biological approach often uses brain imaging techniques.
Cognitive psychology studies internal mental processes like problem-solving.
The sociocultural approach highlights the role of shared cultural knowledge.
No single approach is accepted as the only explanation for human behaviour.

quiz.say: A psychologist studies how language acquisition differs between children raised in different languages.
quiz.why: This focuses on how the surrounding culture shapes the learning process.

wrong.0: This would focus on the physical brain areas responsible for language.
wrong.1: This would focus only on the internal rules of grammar, not the social context.
wrong.2: This approach focuses only on observable actions, not cultural rules.

quiz.say: A researcher maps the correlation between a specific gene and aggression levels.
quiz.why: This directly examines the physical, genetic makeup of the individual.

wrong.0: This ignores the environmental or social factors.
wrong.1: This old theory focuses on unconscious drives, not genes.
wrong.3: This ignores the physical basis of the trait.

quiz.say: A student struggles to remember names, but their ability to solve complex math problems remains high.
quiz.why: This comparison highlights a specific failure in one mental process, memory.

wrong.0: While biology is involved, the focus is on the process failure, not the physical damage itself.
wrong.1: This doesn't point to a failure related to social learning or culture.
wrong.2: This focuses too narrowly on feelings, ignoring the specific memory task.
